opportunities.name: GitHub candidate sourcing → lead email
opportunities.description: Look up the GitHub user <username>, collect their follower count and top repo's stars and language, then draft a lead email to <recipient> for <role>.
steps: Open github.com and click 'Search or jump to'
Type <username> and press Enter
Click the 'Users' filter in the left sidebar
Open the matching user profile and note the follower count and pinned repos
Open the top repo and note its stars and primary language
Find the latest post or project (blog or pinned item)
Open the mail app and start a new message
Fill To = <recipient>
Fill Subject = 'Lead for <role>: <username>'
Fill Body = '<username>: <followers> followers, top repo <repo> (<stars> stars, <language>), latest post: <latest_post>.'
Send or discard the draft (the person discarded every draft)

instances.values: username=karpathy, role=ML Research Engineer, recipient=hiring@example.com; nanoGPT 63.8k stars, Python, 226k followers
username=gaearon, role=Staff Frontend Engineer, recipient=hiring@example.com; react/react 251k stars, JavaScript, 94k followers
username=simonw (Simon Willison); opened repo 'llm'; no email recorded (incomplete)

opportunities.name: Person + company history research note
opportunities.description: Look up <person> on Wikipedia, check how <company_domain> looked in <year> on the Wayback Machine, then save a summary note.
steps: Open Wikipedia and type <person> in the search box, then press Enter
Note the person's birth date and current role
Open the Wayback Machine and enter <company_domain>
Pick <year> in the timeline and open a snapshot date
Note the headline on the homepage
In the notes app, add a note: '<person>: born <date>, <role>. <company_domain> in <year>: <headline>'

instances.values: person=Tim Berners-Lee; opened the Wayback Machine but entered no domain (incomplete)

opportunities.name: Address nearest-POI walking route + neighborhood note
opportunities.description: Find the <poi_type> nearest to <address> on OpenStreetMap, get walking directions to it, look up <neighborhood> on Wikipedia, and save a summary note.
steps: On OpenStreetMap, search '<poi_type> near <address>' and open the top result
Click 'Find directions', choose Foot mode
Set From = <address> and To = the result name, then press Enter
Note the distance and walking time
Search Wikipedia for <neighborhood> and note a one-line description
Add a note: '<address>: nearest <poi_type> <name>, <distance>, <time> walk. <neighborhood>: <description>'
